introduction: ERC-2098 defines a compact, 64-byte representation of an Ethereum secp256k1 signature, replacing the traditional 65-byte (r, s, v) triplet with two 32-byte words, r and yParityAndS. It was proposed by Richard Moore and Nick Johnson in March 2019. The encoding relies on the top bit of the s value being zero in canonical signatures, so the yParity bit is stored in that free high bit, giving yParityAndS = (yParity << 255) | s. Decoding reverses it to recover r, s, and yParity for ecrecover.
designPurpose: ERC-2098 was designed to shrink signature payloads that waste space and gas. A canonical signature needs 65 bytes, but once padded to 256-bit EVM words it occupies 96 bytes with 31 injected zero bytes, and RLP-encoded transactions spend on average 1.5 extra bytes on yParity. By packing the yParity bit into the always-zero high bit of s, the standard fits a full signature into two aligned 32-byte words, cutting calldata size and the gas cost of passing signatures without losing any information.
commonUsage: Compact signatures are used wherever signatures travel as calldata and space matters: meta-transaction relayers, multi-signature wallets, and permit-style approvals. The ethers.js library exposes the packed form as an internal split-signature property, and recovery utilities accept the (r, yParityAndS) layout alongside the classic (r, s, v) form before calling ecrecover. Because the representation is a pure encoding, it composes with any scheme that already relies on ECDSA signatures.
sim.compactEncoding.name: Compact Signature Encoding
sim.compactEncoding.desc: Follow a signature from canonical (r, s, v) form through compact packing to on-chain recovery.
sim.compactEncoding.step.sign: The signer produces a canonical secp256k1 signature with components r, s, and yParity.
sim.compactEncoding.step.pack: The encoder stores yParity in the top bit of s, producing r and yParityAndS as two 32-byte words.
sim.compactEncoding.step.submit: The 64-byte compact signature is submitted on-chain as the pair (r, yParityAndS).
sim.compactEncoding.step.recover: The verifier unpacks yParity and s from yParityAndS, then calls ecrecover to recover the signer address.
